_what: Publishing a site at its own address (read-data/site-addresses.mjs). A site's files are kept in the person's own files under `files_folder`/<installation>/ (the engine's computer answers them, trillion-rust src/native_entry/computer/installations.rs); which host shows which installation is the list in `origins_file`, {origins: [{host, installation, moved_to?}]}, which the person's computer signs with the account's key and hands to the forwarder (trillion-rust src/forwarder/origins.rs). A name is one label under `suffix` (old trillion src/public-app-names.json: `pattern`, `reserved`, `first_words`, `longest`); a renamed site keeps its earlier name, which sends visitors on to the new one (`moved_to`). A person's own domain is believed once its TXT record `proof_label`.<domain> holds `proof_value_prefix` + the account's address, and reaches the forwarder through the address record pointing at `points_at`. `installation_hex` is the length of an installation id. `most_origins` bounds the list (the forwarder's own bound). `piece_bytes` is how much one written piece carries. `words` are every refusal and answer. `told_file` is where the person's computer keeps what the forwarder answered the list with; `words.refusals` says each of the forwarder's refusal words (trillion-rust src/forwarder/words.json) in plain words.

words.refused: A name is 3 to 40 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, like field-notes.
words.reserved: That name is kept for Trillion. Choose another.
words.taken: Another of your sites already uses that address. Choose another, or let it go first.
words.no_name: Give a name, or a title to make one from.
words.installation: Give the installation as its 32-character id (publish_site answers it).
words.not_published: That installation has no files yet: publish the site first.
words.domain: Give a domain you own with a valid top-level name, like shop.example.com.
words.domain_is_name: That is a site name, not your own domain: use name_site for it.
words.account: Give your account's address: the 64 characters after /a/ in your Trillion address.
words.too_many: A site list holds at most 64 addresses. Let one go first.
words.unknown_host: None of your sites uses that address.
words.site: Give the site as files by path (index.html first), or the name of a site.json in your files, such as one copy_a_site left.
words.live_when: Your computer hands the new address to the forwarder within a few seconds; it answers while your computer is on. Publish the site again to list its pages for AI apps at its new address (llms.txt).
words.domain_when: Add both DNS records at your domain's DNS host; the address answers once the TXT record is visible and a certificate is made for it.

refusals.host_taken: Another account's site holds one of these addresses. Choose another name, or let that address go.
refusals.domain_unproven: A domain's TXT record is not visible yet. Add it as attach_domain said; it is checked again when your computer next connects.
refusals.name_reserved: One of these names is kept for Trillion. Choose another.
refusals.origins_stale: A newer list was handed in already.
refusals.origins_full: The forwarder holds as many accounts' sites as it can just now. Try again later.
refusals.origins_not_believed: Your computer was not connected when it handed the list in; it tries again.
